In Zanzibar, harees is called **boko boko**, also spelled "bokoboko". It's a meat and cracked-wheat porridge, usually made with beef.

Support for this is mixed. The Kenyan Standard recipe says the dish is known as harees in the Middle East and that Middle Eastern settlers brought it to the East African coast. Al Jazeera's street-food feature names bokoboko as a signature Zanzibar dish. The Arrival Guides listing for Al-Jabry in Zanzibar Town describes boko-boko as a meat porridge soup. None of these sources states outright that boko boko is Zanzibar's name for harees, so that link is my inference from them. I didn't open the Wikipedia article on Harees itself, so I can't say whether it gives this name.
